If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative over 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–3% for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect trend reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 1–1.5% for early horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 1–1.5% for mid horizon to avoid underestimating downside risk.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below 70% of recent high, increase forecast by 1–2% for late horizon to capture momentum continuation.
